title: EU Renews Assad-Era Sanctions, Delists Syria's Defence and Interior Ministries
detail: The EU Council renewed restrictive measures against individuals and entities linked to the former Assad regime until June 1, 2027, while simultaneously removing seven entities from the sanctions list — most significantly Syria's Ministries of Defence and Interior as they now operate under the transitional government of Ahmad al-Sharaa. The delisting enables direct EU engagement with Syria's new security architecture and opens the door for security sector cooperation. This followed the May 11 restoration of the full EU-Syria Cooperation Agreement (suspended since 2011). The combined moves mark the most significant EU normalization steps with Damascus in over a decade. Enab Baladi reported that the EU's approach distinguished between the former regime's structures (still sanctioned) and the new transitional administration (now eligible for engagement).

title: Al-Sharaa Appoints Safwat Raslan as New Central Bank Governor
detail: Syrian transitional President Ahmad al-Sharaa appointed Safwat Raslan — previously head of the Syrian Development Fund — as the new Governor of the Central Bank of Syria. The outgoing governor, Abdelkader Husriyeh, was appointed as Syria's ambassador to Canada. The reshuffle signals a move to bring technocratic reform to Syria's banking sector, which has been paralyzed by international sanctions and the collapse of the Syrian pound (SYP). The appointment came weeks after US sanctions waivers and EU normalization steps created space for international banking re-engagement. Stabilizing the central bank is considered a precondition for attracting the foreign investment Syria needs for reconstruction.
